purpose: Read-only host readiness reassessment after both E08 timing observations were contaminated; no operational workload or host configuration change.
execution_note: The executed command supplied the saved script body through a quoted SSH stdin heredoc. This equivalent file-input command is for reproduction; no second capture was run.
duration_note: One initial process/core baseline followed by eleven five-second intervals, not twelve samples. Elapsed includes procfs/process collection overhead.

topology.read_command: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 minimax 'lscpu -e=CPU,CORE,SOCKET,MAXMHZ; lscpu | sed -n "1,20p"'
topology.model: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S
topology.note: lscpu provides no distinct efficiency/performance core classes here. Fixture CPUs 8–15 and siblings 24–31 are physical cores 8–15; observed KVM vCPU interval-end snapshots were on the other physical-core set.

limitations: Max-per-core prelaunch quiet differs from in-run foreign CPU: the driver sums fixture-core running time, subtracts role CPU and ksoftirqd, then compares with 0.05 × occupied seconds. Passing ninety seconds of per-core quiet cannot prove aggregate in-run validity.
Summed fixture CPU here is descriptive raw schedstat running time; it does not subtract observer CPU or ksoftirqd and is not the driver foreign-CPU metric.

Process CPU uses /proc stat tick deltas for surviving processes. Threads provide interval-end last-CPU snapshots and permitted masks, not exact CPU residency or causal attribution of the earlier failed observations.
QEMU remains active and may run on any CPU 0–31. Current quiet placement does not constrain future migration when the fixture starts.
This observation did not reproduce a large fixture-core burst. The earlier actual foreign-CPU measurements remain the evidence that thirty-second prelaunch quiet missed interference.
recommendation: One same-binary replacement pair after a separately recorded ninety-second supplemental quiet observation using the existing 0.05 per-core threshold and 7200-second bound is a proportionate finite validity refinement. Keep the archived driver, affinities and acceptance/contamination criteria unchanged. If that replacement is contaminated, stop E08 timing retries and reassess scheduling or an external dependency; do not keep increasing the quiet window.
